assets.video.bitrate.mode.matched: the video essence in the file must be encoded as AVC Intra Class 100 as defined by SMPTE RP 2027:2011. This equates to an actual video essence data rate of approximately 113Mbits/s
assets.video.bitrate.mode.note: AVC-Intra Class 100 (SMPTE RP 2027) is an intra-frame-only codec defined with a fixed target bitrate per its governing standard; the document states an approximate data rate rather than the word 'constant'. Derived from the codec's defining standard, not a literal string match — flagged for human review.

assets.video.color.range[0].matched: each component is allowed to range between 0 and 100% (or 0mV and 700mV). This equates to digital sample levels 16 and 235 (8-bit systems) or 64 and 940 (10 bit systems)
assets.video.color.range[0].note: 16-235 (8-bit) / 64-940 (10-bit) is the broadcast legal/limited signal range as opposed to full range (0-255/0-1023); the document states the numeric levels but never uses the word 'limited' itself, hence method=model not literal. Same source text underlies the already-recorded constraints.video.signal_limits.luminance/rgb min/max (64/940) in this file.

assets.video.signal.field_order[0].matched: Cuts in material must happen on frame boundaries (i.e. between field 2 and field 1). Motion on psf material must always occur between field 2 and field 1 (i.e. field 1 dominance)
assets.video.signal.field_order[0].note: the document specifies 'field 1 dominance' for 1080i/25 material but never uses the term 'top field first'. By the standard 1080i line-numbering convention, field 1 is the field containing the first (topmost) line, so field-1-dominance corresponds to top-field-first — an inference from the cited field-dominance rule plus external 1080i convention, not a literal string match. Flagged for human review.

assets.audio.codec.disallowed[1].matched: All audio tracks must be encoded as PCM with a sample rate of 48kHz at a depth of 24bits/sample
assets.audio.codec.disallowed[1].note: the document names PCM as the sole required audio codec (section 4.4) but never names MP3 individually. mp3 is treated as disallowed here as one of the non-PCM codecs excluded by the PCM-only requirement — same reasoning already applied to the aac entry at disallowed[0] in this file, not a literal match.
